utterances.text: From the same firing positions that were mentioned until now, namely Zarkovica, Bosanka, and Srdj, I calculated the dispersion patterns in respect of the following targets: Anti-aircraft gun, about 150 to 200 metres to the north of the walls of the Old Town. Secondly, as for a target, the anti-aircraft gun at the beginning of the funicular, or cable car. And the anti-aircraft gun east of Ploce about 200 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, before you continue, sir, I'd like to give you map -- or show you map P160 again, and could you please show the Court which three guns, anti-aircraft guns, you're referring to. If you could place that on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I apologise for interrupting the witness and my learned colleague. I see only one of the calculations that my colleague has referred to, Mr. Weiner. It's the calculation that has to do with the gun north of the Old Town. I do not see the other three that he mentions in his question that starts on page 22, line 25. I see only one in the material that was disclosed to us. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: All right. Why don't we do this: Why don't we hand the supplement out, which was disclosed to you, and then we can have the witness look at the supplement and explain the supplement, number one, as well as show you on the map what he's referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner, how long do you think that exercise would take?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Just three or four minutes --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Mr. Weiner, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Five minutes at the most.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: When were you planning to take the next break, Your Honour, so I can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Any time in the next five or six minutes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Why don't we do this: If we can take the break now, when the witness comes back, he will have everything in front of him and I'll also meet with Defence counsel to make sure we're on the same page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That's why I asked the question. We will have a break now, and everything will be in order when we return.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: We're all on the same page. It was just they were looking at the wrong document. Speaking of documents, very quickly, could the witness be shown this table, pages 106 and 107.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Colonel Poje, are these tables the ones that you referred to about 30 minutes ago when you were discussing the first hypothetical in the addendum, on page 4, and you told us about the Vd of 14 and the Vp of 10? Are these the tables that you were discussing?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, these are the tables.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'd like to offer that at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The exhibit will be marked P182.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, if you could please provide supplement number 1 to the witness and to the other parties.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Colonel Poje, looking at supplement number 1, did you calculate some hypothetical situations where JNA mortars, if firing at Croatian anti-aircraft guns, whether or not it would have had projectile dispersion into the Old Town? Did you make certain calculations about that?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: Yes, I did make calculations for those three examples that are given there, the three anti-aircraft guns north of the Old Town at the beginning, where the cable car starts, and east of Ploce.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Actually, the -- it's one gun north of the Old Town with two different positions. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: Yes. One of them is about 150 to 200 metres away from the walls of the Old Town, at the beginning of the cable car.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I just want to -- before we look on the map, I just want to get it straight. In your hypotheticals, JNA mortars would be firing from what locations, according to your calculations in supplement 1?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: I made the calculation from several firing positions. The first one was in Zarkovica, the second was at Bosanka, and I also took a third example of a position on Srdj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, using the map to your right, which is Exhibit P160, could you please show us where those target positions are; the one anti-aircraft gun in two different positions north of the Old Town, and the other location to the east of the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: This is one position. It's north of Old Town, assuming that the same gun is also located at the beginning of the cable car. And the third position is this position.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, for the record, the witness was pointing at the symbol above the Old Town, to the top of the symbol. He then pointed to a second position approximately, I would say, one-half inch, but I would have to get that in centimetres --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would ask my learned colleague to precisely describe what the witness indicated. So the symbol, for example, that is mentioned is on the walls of the Old Town, which can be clearly seen, and he indicated two or three inches - I'm not quite familiar with inches and I apologise because of that - pointed to the north, to the beginning of the cable car, so that he did not precisely point out what can be seen on the map. I apologise again for interrupting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Rather than letting me try and convert inches to centimetres, I'll have him write numbers on the three locations, with the Court's permission, if he can write on the map the numbers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is that map an exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That produces a problem, I'm told.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: All right. We can see the symbol. Okay. We won't write it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, we can see the symbol above the Old Town, the anti-aircraft symbol above the Old Town. How far, in centimetres, is the cable car line?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, for the record, I would like my learned friend to explain to me how this symbol can be above the Old Town. The bottom part touches the houses, the middle is on the actual wall. So how can he see it above and outside of the Old Town? I would like to see, and I would like an explanation of how my colleague sees that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Are you going to make any comment on that, or are you going to change your tack, or are we going to get to the foot of the cable car?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: We can get to the foot of the cable car.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, can you tell us, from the Old Town walls, approximately how far is the foot of the cable car?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: About 300 to 350 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you made your calculations, how far was the anti-aircraft gun from the Old Town? The second one, the one closest to the Old Town walls, how far was that gun from the Old Town when you made your calculations?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: When I was making my calculations, I took that -- the anti-aircraft gun to be at the top of the arrow.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And why did you do that, sir?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: As far as I can recall, anti-aircraft cannon would be indicated -- the top of the arrow would not indicate the place of the anti-aircraft gun.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The top of the arrow would not or would indicate the place? I'm sorry, I --

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: It would mark it, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, is having an anti-aircraft gun backing up to a wall, is that a good position for situating an anti-aircraft gun, with its back to the wall?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: It's probably not good, because it doesn't have the area to be covered, because we know that an anti-aircraft gun is primarily meant to fire at aircraft. So a position placing it near a wall would not be a favourable position for such a weapon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in map drawing practice, where you have the anti-aircraft gun symbol, where is the anti-aircraft gun itself located?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: As far as I know, at the top of the arrow indicating that gun.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where is the third location that you referred to?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: I said that it was to the east by 200 metres from the mortar position in the Ploce sector.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, did you prepare those calculations listed in addendum number 2 -- I'm sorry, addendum number 1, these seven pages? I'm sorry, not addendum, supplement number 1. Did you prepare that?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you briefly explain what they are, since they're not in English, they're being translated right now.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: The procedure to calculate the dispersion pattern is the same as in the previous case which I explained. There is no other way of calculating it but on the basis of the determined firing distance, the chosen charge, then we determine the deflections by direction and by distance, and then based on that we calculate the semi-axis of the dispersion ellipses, and that is how we calculate the area covered by the dispersion zone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you use those tables that you had shown us previously, those pages 106 and 107? Did you use those same tables in calculating the dispersion ellipses?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: Yes, I used those tables, but I used those pages which correspond to the specific charge and the firing distance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And are those the same tables in that 1985 book that you had? Are those the same tables that were used in the fall of 1991 by the JNA?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And considering each of these calculations or evaluations, do any of the semi-axes of the dispersion ellipses enter or overlap with the Old Town? Do any of them?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: The dispersion ellipses that I calculated and cited, the dispersion pattern ranges from 40 to 160 metres. The semi-axes of the dispersion pattern are in the boundaries from 20 to 80 metres. In view of those places where the targets were not located, no dispersion zone or semi-axis of dispersion would approach or overlap with the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Colonel, did you ever calculate the hypothetical situation of whether JNA mortars, if firing from Uskoplje, would have any projectile dispersion if it was firing into the Old Town from that same anti-aircraft location?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: I did make one calculation if firing was carried out from a battalion firing group based on the map which was shown to me at the beginning after the first break, from the Uskoplje position, using 120-millimetre mortars.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: The dispersion pattern, or the semi-axis of dispersion for that example, for that distance, 5.600 metres, which was the approximate firing distance, would be 140 by 86 [as interpreted] metres. We could say on this example that 1 to 2 per cent of the hits could fall on the walls of the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown supplement number 2, please. Now, could the witness be shown map 132, where he can show us the positions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you show us Uskoplje and your target, Colonel.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: This is the firing position of the battalion artillery or firing group 3. The target, we said, is 150 metres to the north of the walls.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what type of mortars did you use?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: 120 millimetres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you make the determination also, the calculation with an 82-millimetre mortar?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: 82-millimetre mortars from that area, from Uskoplje, was within range. So I didn't calculate that, there was no need to do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you mean it was within range, the 82-millimetre mortar?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: The 82, from its positions on the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter is not clear whether the witness is saying that it is within range or it is not within range.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Colonel, we're having an interpretation problem. The 82-millimetre mortar, is its firing within range of the Old Town or outside of the range of the Old Town in the Uskoplje hypothetical?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: The 82 -- the 82 mortars could not reach the Old Town. They did not have the range to reach the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, assuming that the 120-millimetre mortars were firing at a hypothetical anti-aircraft gun approximately 150 metres north of the Old Town, what's your conclusion as to projectile dispersion? What was your conclusion in supplement number 2?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: As I said, the dispersion pattern in that example ranges from 280 to 152 metres. The semi-axis of the dispersion is 140 by 76 metres. So that is the dispersion from the average trajectory closer to the town. We can say that in that example, 1 to 2 per cent of the hits could fall on the walls of the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you say "could," is that a possibility or is that a definite situation?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: If we said that the target was 150 metres away from the walls and the semi-axis dispersion was 140, then the position of the cannon could have been 140 metres or 130 metres. So there is a possibility that a small percentage of the projectiles hit the walls. It's not possible directly because we still have 10 metres remaining, 140 or 150. When we're talking about the distance alone, then we could have an error of 10 to 20 metres which could result in, as I wrote down, 1 to 2 per cent of all projectiles that were fired, hypothetically, on that target could also hit the walls of the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that due to the effect of distance on the ellipse? You expand the ellipse because of distance?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: The ellipse is such -- such as it was calculated, 250 by 152, could be by also 140 by 76 metres. Increasing the distance by 50 metres up or down would not significantly change the dispersion pattern. Perhaps it could affect it by 1 or 2 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now I would like you to go to the next map --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Before you move, Mr. Weiner, on this second supplement, I noticed firstly that on the B/C/S version the ellipse is shown as 280 by 152 metres, yet the paragraph immediately following the table it's shown as 280 by 156 metres. There's a 4 metre discrepancy there. On the English version, the table, that dimension was illegible, and yet the 156 is repeated in the written paragraph that follows. Can we be sure whether it is 152 or 156?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Colonel Poje, can you look at the supplement number 2, in the B/C/S version. In the bottom of your table, you say 280 by 152. In the sentence below that, it says 280 by 156.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: It's probably my typing error, because 76 times 2 is 152 metres. Probably I wrote down 156 by mistake.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The second matter is just a note that in the transcript at 30, line 11, the dispersion ellipse half axis is shown as 140 by 86 in the transcript, whereas it's clearly 140 by 76 on the table.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that correct, sir? Should it be 140 by 76?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: The semi-axis of dispersion is 140 by 76 plus/minus.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. On the B/C/S version of supplement number 2, could you correct that and make that a 152 and initial that, please.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was going to move all the documents in at the end. Is that all right with you, or would you rather have me move them in one at a time? There's only three or four.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, could we now look at map P160. Now, sir, do you see where Gradac Park is located on that map?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: Could you please guide me in a way?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Approximately 300 metres to the left of the Old Town. Area to the west of the Old Town. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if the witness knows how to find something on a map, he will do so. The way in which my learned friend is doing this is leading, I believe. The question is how he could write such a report if he cannot find this on the map. But anyway, putting this kind of question is wrong.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Petrovic, I can't agree with you on this occasion. The witness is being directed to a point on a map that has been identified in the course of evidence. If we left him to his own devices, we could be here at 7.00 finding it. Any witness can have that bother. I can look at a map and not see --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the Presiding Judge, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: So we won't be too persnickity about this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, based on your previous calculations of firing from JNA forces from Zarkovica, if they fired from Zarkovica toward or on any target in Gradac Park, are the error of probabilities -- I'm sorry -- are the semi-axes of the dispersion ellipse, would those overlap into the Old Town or enter the Old Town if you're firing from Zarkovica onto Gradac Park?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: If one shoots from Zarkovica to the Gradac Park, the ellipses does not overlap the Old Town, does not coincide with it.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please be asked to speak into the microphone the interpreters note.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And what's your basis of that answer?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: On the basis of all the calculations that I made for different targets around town, around the town. Not in a single calculation did I get such a big ellipse of dispersion that it encompassed part of the town or that it went through town.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm sorry for interrupting my colleague. I do not have any calculation for the Gradac Park. Perhaps again we have a mistake here. Where is this calculation for Gradac Park, the one that the witness is talking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I was just asking him to calculate based on his previous calculations. There is no discovery in use. And counsel also said again we have a problem here. The last time they did have the proper discovery, they were just looking at the wrong page. So this is not the second time there's been any problem. May I continue? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a question on ellipses and dispersion error. The farther that you fire from a location towards a target, is the percentage of error, does that increase? Does that have any effect on the dispersion error, the greater the distance that you fire?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: With one charge, as the distance is increased, the dispersion pattern goes up too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, sir, I've got a couple questions on other matters in your report. You didn't mention recoilless cannons or tanks firing in your findings. If they had fired on the 6th of December, would that have changed your conclusions or opinions?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: It would not have changed them. I've already mentioned, inter alia, that I used the reports of the Yugoslav Army and UNESCO, and there is no mention there of any impacts coming from cannons, recoilless cannons and tanks. I cannot confirm this with 100 per cent certainty, that is, that they were not fired from.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But, sir, assuming that they were used, would that change any of your calculations or your findings or conclusions?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: A recoilless gun and tanks engage in direct fire. So as far as that is concerned, they are more precise and more accurate than mortar fire which is indirect fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So are the error probabilities of direct weapons greater or less than that of mortars?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: The dispersion pattern is considerably lower in the case of direct fire than in the case of indirect fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Colonel Poje, have you been to the Old Town of Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And have you walked through the streets and reviewed the area?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: I reviewed it, and I photographed it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is the Old Town -- based on your review or your evaluation of the Old Town, is it suitable for artillery and mortars?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: In view of how densely it is populated, the narrow streets, the relatively high buildings, the Old Town of Dubrovnik is not favourable for artillery and mortar positions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does the ground, the type of ground, the hard surface, does that affect your opinion?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: It does affect it. Actually, when there is a hard surface, and that is stone, the weapon shakes when it is fired, and that is why, of course, that kind of surface is not good for choosing that kind of position.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would the use of sandbags correct the problem in the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: As far as the surface is concerned where the weapons would be, then that problem could be resolved with sandbags, but I think there's another problem involved too. The narrow streets, the high buildings, the question where such a position could be found from which one could fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With sandbags, would you still have recoil problems, shaking problems?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: Probably, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is that a danger to the soldiers operating the mortars if it's shaking, and recoil problems?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: There is a danger, though not a major one. For example, a mortar can simply fall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Colonel Poje, are you familiar with the anti-aircraft weapons?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: Let's say a little bit. I'm not an expert in anti-aircraft artillery. I am familiar with it to a degree.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are there various types of anti-aircraft weaponry?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: Yes, there are. There are anti-artillery systems -- anti-aircraft systems that are guns and anti-aircraft systems that are rockets.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what are they used for?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: As the name says itself, there are barrel-based systems and rocket-based systems that are used for targeting aircraft and helicopters and other targets that are in the air.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can it also be used to target, or it also be used for targets on the ground?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: Cannon systems like three-barrelled, or single-barrelled anti-aircraft guns to be used for targets on the ground, but rocket systems cannot be used. These are rockets that are guided.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And are these direct-fire systems?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: It involves direct fire. These are direct-fire systems.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, based on your analysis or your review of the Old Town, is the Stradun a good place for an anti-aircraft weapon?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: In view of the fact that on the Stradun both left and right and front and back, there are relatively, I say relatively, high buildings, that would mean that an anti-aircraft weapon, a cannon, for instance, would cover a relatively small area in the air. That means that it would not be a very favourable position for anti-aircraft artillery.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it make a difference if it was an anti-aircraft weapon on a vehicle or standing alone? Does it make a difference?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: Frankly speaking, so far, if we are talking about three-barrelled or one-barrel guns of 20 millimetres, I haven't seen any such thing. I cannot say yes or no by way of an answer, whether it's possible to place this kind of gun on a vehicle, to mount it on a vehicle and to be used as an anti-aircraft gun from such a position. Even if it were to be mounted, let us assume that - I've never even any such thing, I've never seen it - probably the vehicle would have to have special stabilisers because it would be very hard for the vehicle to be stable enough on wheels.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about firing an anti-aircraft weapon from the walls?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: The walls are relatively narrow, and it would be hard to place such a cannon there. It is possible, hypothetically, to position it on a somewhat broader part of the walls, but then there's the problem of how the gun could be brought to that position, and also the question of the stability of the walls themselves when shooting, when firing. I don't know what the stability is. So the question is whether the walls could take that kind of activity such as the firing of a three-barrelled anti-aircraft gun.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll get back to the walls in a few minutes, but what about the anti-aircraft guns called the Strela or Igla? Are you familiar with those?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you fire one of those from inside a building?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: As far as all rocket systems are concerned, one does not shoot from indoors, from within a building. We know what rocket systems are like, and we know that rocket motors have to be out in the open or otherwise they would cause damage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "damage," if you fired it indoors --

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: Fire. It means that a fire can break out. It's enormous flames that one sees when a rocket is launched. That's what creates it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, these Strelas and Iglas, are these heat-seeking weapons?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And these heat-seeking projectiles, are they used against ground troops?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: Such projectiles are actually those that require a powerful source of heat or energy, and it's very hard to find such a source.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. When I say ground troops, what about other land objects?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: In principle, no. These are systems that are intended for targeting aircraft only.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you indicated that there is a possibility of -- although a difficult possibility, of firing an anti-aircraft gun from the walls. If you fire an anti-aircraft gun from the walls, is it visible?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: 20-millimetre ammunition that is used for an anti-aircraft gun is a very noticeable one. It has a tracer. It makes it easier for the gunner to target aircraft, for instance, in the air, because it can follow the actual flight of the projectile since the speed is relatively big - of the firing, that is - and if there were no tracer, the gunner would probably not even notice, would not even see the direction where it went.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are these tracers quite visible in the sky?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: Tracers are visible. That's why they exist in the first place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if you're firing one of these guns with tracer bullets, aren't you an easy target?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: I have already mentioned that for the most part these guns are used for targeting aircraft.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But if you fire it from the walls, due to the tracers do you become an easy target because the tracers can be observed?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: Most definitely. Most definitely. Hypothetically, if one were to fire from the walls or from anyplace with these guns, the location from where the firing takes place can certainly be seen, and such a weapon becomes a target.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if the Old Town was being filmed or video recorded during a shelling and anti-aircraft guns were firing from the town, would tracers be visible on this film?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: They should be visible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just one question apparently didn't come out on the -- or it just came up partially on the transcript. If you're firing one of those heat-seeking rockets, one of those anti-aircraft rockets, is a lot of heat necessary for the rocket to target a certain object?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: I don't know how much, but I imagine a considerable amount is required. I don't know what the exact figure would be.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And does the projectile move towards an object emanating heat?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, sir, I'd like you to look at your report. There are a couple answers that I want to ask you about. Question 18 b) -- or answer 18 b). Could you read that, please.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: "Weapons used to attack Dubrovnik."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Read that to yourself, please. Sir, could you explain that? You make two or three points in that. Could you explain what you mean?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: Are we talking about the same question, 18 b)?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: In the first part, I claim that the Yugoslav Army did not have the intention of taking the town, because according to the decision of the 2nd of December, the deployment of the 3rd Battalion is a defensive one. It is positioned for defence. That can be seen on the map. Secondly, I claim that all the objectives or, rather, targets that can be seen would be directly targeted, those that can be seen from the positions of the Yugoslav People's Army in Dubrovnik and around Dubrovnik. So they would be targeted by direct fire. The other targets would be engaged by mortar fire. And the last thing I say is that only those buildings from which people fire are targeted, in principle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: If that cannot be stopped in any other way, if this gunfire coming from them cannot be stopped in some other way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you were talking about the Old City. Were you referring to any targets within the Old City?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: As far as I know, there were no targets in the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you mean by JNA doctrine? "... populated areas fire is directed only against buildings from which people fire..." What do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: That means that if fire was coming from a building, it's possible to fire at that building if in some other way it's not possible to make sure that the firing stops from that particular building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you mention that the troops around Dubrovnik were in a defensive position. Is that the same as also being in a blockading position?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: Well, you could say that to a certain extent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, 18 d). Could you look at that, please, that answer. That ERN number that you referred to and certain information from it, 0600 hours, Croatian forces, forces of the JNA 3rd Motorised Battalion, the 11.15 cease-fire ordered by General Strugar, where did you get that information, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: In the documents that I reviewed, especially the radiogram documents. I found that in the radiograms that what is stated here is mentioned two or three times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that radiogram, do you know who sent it?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: As far as I know, it -- according to the document, it's a radiogram by General Strugar.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, what is that exhibit? What document are we talking about? Has that already been admitted into evidence, or which document is that? Could we please find out which document we're talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: It has the ERN number, that's the radiogram between General Strugar and, I believe, Mr. Rudolf. The one that Mr. Rudolf discussed and the one that also Mr. Hvalkof discussed. It's in Mr. Hvalkof's daily diary of times, and it's also discussed by Mr. Rudolf. It is in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, yes, but it's not General Strugar. The Rudolf radiograms refer to General Jokic. So that is part of the exhibits of this case. If there is some other exhibit, then, please, we'd like to be told.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: It's the exhibit in evidence which indicates that General Strugar has called for a cease-fire at 11.15. I would be happy to provide the document tomorrow morning, if the Court would like.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Perhaps you can clarify with Mr. Petrovic the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, is there a mortar technique that's used if you want to fire at a target that is close to a protected object?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: If the targets are close to a protected object or if they are close to one's own units, the initial firing, the correction, would start at the point which is away, on the side which is away from the protected facility, with the assumption that the first projectile should not hit the protected facility.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what do you do with any subsequent projectile?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: And when you have a first hit, then you start getting closer and closer to the actual target until you hit the centre of the target.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you kind of creep up on the target, if you want to --

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: Yes. We use such an example in order to avoid damage or destruction of the protected building or harm to our own unit. So you approach the target gradually.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, in your report you indicated that it was possible that the Croats fired into the Old Town, but you said on page 27 that the chances of this were, and I quote: "Very small and above all theoretical." Why do you believe that there was little or no chance of the Croats shelling the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: If we take into account the deployment of the JNA forces, Zarkovica, Bosanka, and in the depth of the territory, only a gross error in targeting those targets would result in hits on the Old Town. The probability is very small, because the trajectories from the positions of the Croatian forces towards the mentioned targets in Zarkovica and Bosanka do not go over the Old Town, but they go to the left of the Old Town. I would like to repeat that: Only a gross error could lead to projectiles or a projectile hitting the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned Zarkovica and Bosanka firing toward the JNA forces on those two places. What about if you're firing upon Mount Srdj?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: I don't know whether the JNA was at Srdj. If it was there and Srdj was fired upon, Srdj is even more to the left of the Old Town, and from those positions, especially mortar positions, it's practically impossible for shells to fall on the town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Speaking of shelling, let's discuss the persons known as fire executors or fire controllers for mortars. Are you familiar with that term?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: We usually call those people who execute the firing. That is a person who determines the place of the target from an observation point, issues the command to fire, monitors or observes the initial firing, makes corrections, certain deviations and corrections until an average projectile would hit the centre of the target. When an average shot would then reach the centre of the target, then group firing would begin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, would those persons, those fire executors or controllers, are they the ones who order the group firing? Are they the ones who order the adjustments and the changes and modifications?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: Fire executors are people who directly issued the order to commence firing. Somebody has to instruct them to fire. They do not decide by themselves to execute the fire. They do not decide when and what they will fire at.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say someone must -- someone must decide when and what they'll fire at, they themselves do not execute the fire, are you talking about the people, the operators of the mortars? Someone has to decide for them?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that's the role of these --

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: A mortar unit does not decide by itself what it will fire at and when it will fire. It has to receive orders to do so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, do these fire executors or fire controllers, do they use any special equipment to aid them in their work?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: Fire executors, in order to execute the firing, uses the equipment and the instruments of communications. Reconnaissance instruments. He uses an artillery compass, a laser target finder. It also uses a plotting circle, a map, a hand compass, binoculars. He also uses communications means to receive commands at the position.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner, I might have to ask you to finish off the tendering of documents, et cetera, in the morning, given the hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will adjourn for the evening. If you would be able, Mr. Poje, to be present tomorrow morning at 9.00. Thank you.
